teams.heading: Hansen says Mark Nawaqanitawase would be better off playing for Fiji
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase's Test allegiance remains open, with no formal commitment to Australia or Fiji in today's coverage. Sir Steve Hansen's view is that the winger 'would be better off playing for Fiji', while a Wallabies captain's verdict on his future is blunt: 'It's pretty obvious'. Each position is a view, not a declaration. Australian coverage meanwhile reports Wallabies salivating over his rugby return.

teams.heading: Exeter boss Rob Baxter backs uncapped Fisilau for England's Nations Championship
teams.body: Exeter's Greg Fisilau, uncapped at 23 and in Steve Borthwick's squad for this month's Nations Championship matches, would adapt well to Test rugby, according to his club boss. Baxter says the number eight's strength is getting in and around the ball, and expects that to carry up a level. He has started every Premiership and European match for Exeter this season and scored seven league tries last season.

lead.why: It is the only England selection item in the pack that is not a repeat of the Mitchell injury or the Edwards rejection, and it concerns a named squad member.

teams.heading: Kitshoff tips Les Bleus as the Springboks' biggest hurdle this month
teams.body: Former Springboks prop Steven Kitshoff, speaking on the For The Love Of Rugby: South Africa podcast, says France will be the biggest hurdle in the Springboks' European leg and the match making South Africans most nervous. He expects a battle of attrition, with tactical kicking and a contest of who can outsmart whom rather than a set-piece shootout. Ben Youngs, the former England scrumhalf, argues Les Bleus must shake off the psychological scars of their Marseille win over the Boks in 2022.

lead.why: The freshest France-focused item, with concrete detail, while the squad-addition story largely repeats Tuesday's Graou lead.

teams.heading: Luke Fitzgerald tips Sam Prendergast ahead of Ciaran Frawley for Argentina
teams.body: Fitzgerald, a 34-times capped Ireland winger and 2009 Lions winger, rates Sam Prendergast as 'a nose in front' of Ciaran Frawley, citing his attacking play and defensive improvement despite kicking figures that have not been spectacular. He also floats Cian Prendergast for the back row with Caelan Doris absent, and argues Frawley's week-in, week-out Connacht form makes him valuable with the World Cup looming.

lead.why: A fresh pundit verdict on the No. 10 selection debate for Friday, with named players and a concrete view on Prendergast versus Frawley.

teams.heading: Quesada calls up former Pumas flyhalf Domingo Miotti for Springboks Test
teams.body: Montpellier flyhalf Domingo Miotti, a former Argentina Test player, is in Quesada's squad for Saturday's Test against the Springboks, his first call-up. He qualifies through an Italian grandfather and last played for Los Pumas on 9 July 2022, which is the basis of his eligibility. Quesada said: "Domingo is a great player and an excellent person." The call gives Quesada four flyhalf options alongside Paolo Garbisi, Tommaso Allan and Giacomo Da Re, and Miotti, who missed last week with injury, can now resume training as normal.

teams.heading: Dafydd Jenkins joins Wales camp with knee issue, Exeter expect no long-term problem
teams.body: Wales lock Dafydd Jenkins has gone into camp for Saturday's match against Japan, with Exeter handing his medical care to the international staff. Jenkins missed Exeter's 31-28 defeat to Harlequins and was also absent from Wales' summer programme through injury. Scans showed bone bruising and some swelling on a piece of cartilage, and Exeter director of rugby Rob Baxter says they do not expect a long-term problem. Steve Tandy's squad includes 14 England-based players, and Jenkins is one of the Exeter contingent he will be relying on.

lead.why: A new Wales squad item with named players and a concrete injury update on a lock who is in camp for the Japan test.

teams.heading: Ignacio Calles called up to Argentina XV after Bernasconi knock
teams.body: Álvaro Galindo has reshaped his Argentina XV for Friday's England A match at Bath after Bautista Bernasconi took a knock in Benetton's URC game against Edinburgh and will not play. The replacement is Ignacio Calles, a 31-year-old Bayonne prop with eight Test caps who has not been picked for Los Pumas in 2026. Benetton front-rower Matías Medrano was also sent off in that same match.

teams.heading: Joe Schmidt, ex-Wallabies boss, says 'a lot at stake' as Nations resumes
teams.body: The former Australia head coach left the role after the Southern Hemisphere Series this summer, and he is now weighing up the wider picture as the inaugural Nations Championship resumes. Speaking to RTÉ Radio 1, Schmidt said "I think there's a lot at stake for the game," and argued that the tournament could draw fans into taking sides. Australia's share of that stake comes at the end of the month, when North v South finals will decide the final standings across both hemispheres, a format Schmidt says he is looking forward to.

lead.why: It is the only NEW shortlist item, and it carries direct on-record comment on the Nations Championship that Australia are part of.

teams.heading: Japan name 35-player squad for the autumn Nations Championship series
teams.body: Wales at Principality Stadium is next, and the 35 names give the management a wide pool to work from. The squad follows a 28-34 defeat to Fiji, their most recent result, and Japan sit 10th of 12 on the log going into that fixture. For a side that has spent this year using a new kick-catch tactic, depth in the squad matters.

teams.heading: Mike Blair says All Blacks head to Murrayfield fully loaded against Scotland
teams.body: New Zealand assistant Mike Blair says the All Blacks will be "fully loaded" for Saturday's Test at Murrayfield, where Scotland are yet to win any of their 33 meetings. Blair, a former Scotland captain, says the last four results between the sides have been close, so the visitors are taking the threat seriously. He also stressed the importance of protecting the record, noting the All Blacks have not lost a Test at Eden Park since 1994.

lead.why: It is a fresh, named coaching statement on the All Blacks' approach to Saturday's Test, and the Cadwallader death has already been covered.

teams.heading: Nick Mallett links Erasmus' full-strength Italy team to All Blacks opener defeat
teams.body: Former Springboks coach Nick Mallett links Erasmus' decision to name his strongest available side for Saturday's Turin test to the Greatest Rivalry series. He traces the opening defeat to the All Blacks in Johannesburg to what he says was "perhaps because of a lack of cohesion in the team." He cannot see Erasmus changing the side much for France and Ireland, with lock Salmaan Moerat recalled and six uncapped players still in the 37-man squad.

lead.why: A new pundit view that explains the full-strength Italy selection, unlike the Erasmus items already reported this week.
